component.name: Roost
component.summary: Organise, tag and find your visual assets

description.p: Roost is a local-first digital asset manager for images, videos, documents and design files. It keeps them in a library on your own disk, and gives you folders, tags, ratings, notes and a fast search over all of them.

ul.li: Thumbnails for photographs, RAW and HEIC, video, PDF, SVG and fonts
Folders and subfolders, tags in groups, ratings, notes and timed comments
Search across names, notes and comments, with filters by tag, rating and type
Files are edited in place by the applications that own them, and Roost notices the save
Imports an existing Eagle library, with its folders, tags and notes

description.p: The library is an open format: the files themselves, and a plain-text journal of everything written about them. Roost needs no account and makes no network connection.

screenshot.caption: A library, with the folders on the left and an asset's details on the right
Every picture at its own proportions, with the details panel hidden
The tags page, with tags arranged in groups

description.p: The frame a video is showing can be copied as a picture.

ul.li: Right-click a video open in the preview and choose Copy this frame: the frame on screen goes to the clipboard at the video's full size, ready to paste into an image editor or a chat.

description.p: A file edited in another application now shows its new contents in the preview straight away.

ul.li: Before, a picture flipped or retouched elsewhere and saved kept its old look in the preview, and in the inspector, until Roost was restarted.
The same holds for HEIC, RAW and TIFF photographs and for the pages of a PDF.

description.p: Markdown and text files can be read and written inside Roost.

ul.li: A .md or .txt file opens in the preview: Markdown is shown formatted, and clicking the text starts editing it there.
While editing Markdown, headings grow and dashes become bullets as you type, and Enter continues a list.
Changes are saved when you press Done, move to the next file or close the preview. A file changed in another application meanwhile is not overwritten.
Markdown and text files get a thumbnail of their first lines.
Add has New Markdown file and New folder.
A file made, imported or pasted inside a folder now goes into that folder, also while a filter is ticked.

description.p: A library left locked by an earlier version opens again.

ul.li: Opening a library no longer fails with "already open in another Roost process" because of a lock an earlier version of Roost left behind.

description.p: Dragging files out works on GNOME, and a closed Roost no longer keeps its library locked.

ul.li: Files dragged out of Roost can be dropped into Files, a browser or a chat app on GNOME. Until now the drop was refused.
Opening a library no longer fails with "already open in another Roost process" when Roost was in fact closed.
Roost finishes closing the library before it quits, whichever way it is closed.
Copies made for Copy file and for dragging no longer pile up on disk: only the latest of each is kept.

description.p: Deleting from a folder keeps what is in another folder too, and a place for files in no folder.

ul.li: Pressing Delete inside a folder takes the files out of that folder. Only a file that is then in no folder at all goes to the trash, and the status bar says which happened.
Right-clicking a file inside a folder offers Remove from that folder, the same as Ctrl+Delete.
Deleting a folder together with its contents leaves alone the files that are also in another folder, and the dialog says how many.
No folder in Places lists every file that is not in any folder yet.

description.p: A view for each kind of place, and a dark title bar.

ul.li: All assets, Recent and your folders each remember their own view: Icons, Compact or Details, the zoom, Show folders and the sort order. Every folder shares one. A place you have not changed yet starts sorted by date added, newest first.
The title bar is dark, matching the window, instead of white on desktops whose theme was not available to Roost.
Videos play with sound. Until now Roost was not allowed to reach the sound server, so every video played silently.

description.p: A fix for the grid after looking at a file.

ul.li: Closing a photograph or a video puts the grid back where you were, instead of near the top. If you stepped to other files while it was open, the grid shows the last one.
A file reached with the arrow keys from below the screen is no longer left cut off by the bottom edge.

description.p: A fix for thumbnails after an import.

ul.li: Pictures imported while the window is open are drawn on screen as soon as they are made. A small file could stay a placeholder until you changed folder.

description.p: The first release from the Digitalku Flatpak repository, which brings updates through your software centre.

ul.li: Thumbnails are drawn as you look at them: what is on screen first, and a file opened or saved elsewhere straight away, instead of the whole library at once.
A photograph taken on its side is drawn and measured upright, the way its orientation tag says.
Refresh thumbnail, in an asset's menu, draws a file's picture again, such as a photograph drawn on its side by 0.1.0.
A search word matches the start of a word, so a partly typed word already finds what it begins.
A folder's own menu calls it New folder.
The grid keeps its place when a selected card changes under it.
